text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

Melbourne journalist RICHARD BIRNIE was born on this day in 1808. At the age of 69 he claimed his "head, stomach, liver, biceps and instep are in fettle to control a whiskey-toddy, digest a haggis and confront life's troubles and cads".
The French founder of the MICHELIN tyre company, ANDRE MICHELIN, was born in 1853.
Australian aviator NIGEL LOVE was born in 1892. He piloted the first paying passenger from Sydney to Melbourne, and eventually married into a flour-milling family before inventing PRO-MAX bread.
Canadian actor ALEXANDER KNOX, whose films included "REACH FOR THE SKY" and "THE SEA WOLF", was born in 1907.
American singer and actress ETHEL MERMAN, who starred in the musicals "ANNIE GET YOUR GUN" and "THERE'S NO BUSINESS LIKE SHOW BUSINESS", was born on this day in 1909.
Australian actress LORRAINE BAYLY was born in 1942. She began her acting career at Sydney's Ensemble Theatre. She gained wide popularity as "Grace" in the television series "The Sullivans".
US country/pop singer JIM STAFFORD was born in 1944. From 1973 onwards he had pop chart successes with hits such as "Spiders and Snakes" (1973), "My Girl Bill" (1974) and "Wildwood West" (1974).

Nigerian-born singer/songwriter SADE (HELEN FOLASADE ADU) was born in 1959. In 1981 she became a member of the band 'Pride' and in 1983 she set up her own backing band. Her hits included "Your Love Is King" (1984), "Smooth Operator" (1984), "Sweetest Taboo" (1985), "Never As Good As The First Time" (1986) and "Paradise" (1988).
** EVENTS **
1547 : IVAN THE TERRIBLE was crowned as the first Tsar of
Russia. He claimed to have deflowered a thousand virgins, and killed as many of his own children.
1809 : The British army under Sir JOHN MOORE defeated a
superior French force at the battle of Corunna, but MOORE was killed in the fighting.
1872 : The ORIENT EXPRESS steamed into Turkey, becoming
the first train to connect the country with Europe.
1920 : Americans raised their glasses for the last time
before the banning of the consumption of alcohol (prohibition) took effect.
1924 : The BBC broadcast the first play, written for
radio, called "DANGER" by RICHARD HUGHES.
1925 : LEON TROTSKY, who once wrote "an ally has to be
watched just like an enemy", was removed from the Communist Party leadership by JOSEPH STALIN and placed under house-arrest.
1932 : DUKE ELLINGTON recorded the hit "IT DON'T MEAN A
THING".
1937 : The DUPONT company patented a "miracle" fibre made
from chemicals, called "nylon".
1942 : American actress CAROLE LOMBARD, wife of CLARK
GABLE, died in a plane crash.
1944 : General EISENHOWER was appointed Supreme Commander
of the Allied Forces in Europe.
1966 : American protest singer JOAN BAEZ was jailed for
10 days after being arrested at an anti-Vietnam demonstration.
1970 : Colonel GADDAFI rose to become Chairman of the
Revolutionary Command Council of Libya.
1979 : American actress and singer CHER filed for
divorce, just 9 days after marrying musician GREG ALLMAN.
1979 : The Shah of Iran left the country after being
forced into exile by Ayatollah Khomeini.
1979 : The "Red bikini girl", who jumped from a Russian

ship in Sydney Harbour was given notice she was likely to be allowed to stay in Australia. The bikini-clad 18-year-old LILLIAN GASINSKAYA was found on a Pyrmont footpath by a photographer. She then went into hiding with friends in Sydney and sought asylum.
1981 : Research into lung cancer found that the death

rate was twice as high in women married to men who smoked 20 or more cigarettes a day than those married to non-smokers. The Takeshi Hirayama National Cancer Research Institute in Tokyo claimed passive smoking had up to half the impact of direct smoking.
1986 : A report into British football violence said
"soccer thugs can never totally be suppressed."
1991 : Allied warplanes bombed Baghdad, at the start of
OPERATION DESERT STORM in the Persian Gulf War, sparked by Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.
1996 : In India, federal police charged seven political
leaders, including six former cabinet ministers, in connection with an $18 million scandal and sought authority to prosecute three ministers in Prime Minister P.V. NARASIMHA RAO's cabinet.
